summary: We developed 1in746, a browser-based educational game. The story begins when a child suddenly wakes up and becomes an astronaut, joining a random mission. During the mission, players must manage limited resources (oxygen, power, food, water, radiation protection, and morale) and complete science activities inspired by real NASA research. The game directly addresses the challenge by letting children experience engineering trade-offs in space missions. Players must decide how to balance radiation protection, power use, and scientific goals across different destinations (ISS, Moon, and Mars). There is no single correct answer—only choices. This project gives children a hands-on way to practice the decisions astronauts face, using real NASA data from DONKI, OSDR, RadLab, Mars Trek, and APOD. To make the game more interesting for children, we also included some fun experiments. The game helps young learners understand that space exploration requires careful choices, teamwork, and scientific thinking.
details:
1in746 is a browser game for all ages, especially for junior kids (teenagers are also welcome). You wake up as an astronaut, get a random job and destination (ISS, Moon, or Mars), then manage oxygen, power, food, water, radiation protection, and morale. Every choice matters. Events and science activities are powered by real NASA data, so your decisions affect whether the crew makes it home.

Players get to practice real space mission trade-offs in a fun, hands-on way. There is no single “right” answer here, only choices and consequences. It’s free, needs no download or login, and works right in the browser.

We want children to feel that space exploration is something they can understand and try. By using real NASA data, the game connects play with actual science and sparks curiosity about becoming part of future missions.

Tools & technologies

Built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Uses NASA APIs and resources including DONKI, APOD, OSDR, RadLab, Mars Trek, and CSA. Help by LLMs such as grok and ChatGPT. Runs in any modern browser.

Creativity & considerations

We designed it so kids experience that space missions are full of trade-offs, not perfect answers. The team focused on simple language, meaningful NASA data use, replayability, and keeping the game encouraging and age-appropriate.
